hero.h1: Copy any post as a card.
hero.sub: Skip the manual crop-and-screenshot routine. Click the button on a post (or press Alt + C) to copy a single post or same-author thread as a crisp 3× card straight to your clipboard, ready to paste anywhere. Twelve materials, rendered entirely on your machine.
hero.meta: Free and open source · GPL-3.0-or-later · Chrome / Edge (Manifest V3, Chrome 111 and later)

guide.h2: How to screenshot a tweet without the clutter
guide.intro: Most people grab a tweet screenshot to share an idea in a deck, newsletter, or group chat—only to end up with reply threads, sidebars, and soft text. There are three common ways to turn a tweet to image, and each carries a clear trade-off.
guide.m1: Press the hardware buttons on iOS or Android, then crop out the status bar, navigation icons, and the first reply underneath. It is fast for a single short post, but the trade-off is fixed screen resolution, uneven margins, and no clean way to capture a multi-post thread without stitching several screenshots together by hand.
guide.m2: Use the OS snipping tool or a browser screenshot shortcut to drag a rectangle around the post on desktop. You get slightly more control over framing than on a phone, yet the trade-off is still display DPI, visible browser chrome or hover states, and re-cropping every time a quote card or photo grid sits near the edge of the viewport.
guide.m3t: Render the post as a card
guide.m3: Instead of photographing pixels off the screen, parse the post’s text, media, and thread structure and lay them out fresh on a clean canvas. The trade-off is that hosted web tools usually ask you to paste a tweet URL into a third-party server, wait on rate-limited APIs, or live with watermarks and broken long threads.
guide.outro: PostPress takes that third approach and runs it entirely inside your browser: click the card button on any X post (or press Alt + C), pick a material, and copy a crisp 3× PNG straight to your clipboard—with replies and ads filtered out, no server, and no login.
guide.imgAlt: A tweet rendered as a clean card in the Midnight material, without browser chrome or replies.
guide.cap: A tweet rendered locally in the Midnight material—no browser chrome, no stray replies.

article.h2: Articles, quotes and image grids survive.
article.lead: An X Article brings out its cover and lead; a quoted post is filled or outlined to suit the material; one to twenty pictures keep their own proportions in the grid, four to a row past the first four (fill crops them square).
article.lede: “Not a filter — paper, rule and type at the right ratio.”
article.s1: Cover, kicker, title and lead come through together.
article.s2: Filled or outlined, following the material.
article.s3: One to twenty keep their own proportions instead of being cropped square; four to a row past the first four, and fill crops them square.

privacy.h2: It runs on your machine, end to end.
privacy.body: No account, no server, no telemetry. Typesetting happens inside an isolated Shadow DOM and the export is drawn by the browser's own canvas. Apart from fetching the pictures already in your card from X's image hosts, nothing leaves the machine.
privacy.note: It does not read your timeline, needs no X account and no X API. Not affiliated with X Corp.
privacy.p1: Puts the finished image on your clipboard, only when you press Copy.
privacy.p2: Remembers your material, canvas and switches; stored locally.
privacy.p3: Fetches the card's pictures. A canvas cannot read cross-origin images without it.

install.lead: Install from the Chrome Web Store in one click; or expand the three-step build from source below.
install.note: Released under GPL-3.0-or-later: redistribute your changes under the same licence.
install.sourceSummary: For developers: build from source (3 steps)
install.s1: Clone the source, install and build. The output lands in dist/.
install.s2: Open chrome://extensions, turn on Developer mode, choose Load unpacked, and pick the dist/ folder.
install.s3: Press the card button on any post (or hover and hit <kbd>Alt</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd>), click Copy Image, and paste anywhere.

faq.lead: Eight real questions, answers on the right.
faq.a1: Cropping a screenshot by hand means dodging replies, stitching long threads across multiple captures, and settling for display DPI and browser chrome. One click on PostPress lays out the whole post or thread to the material's rules and puts a crisp 3× image straight on your clipboard, ready to paste.
faq.q2: Does a long card blur in the feed?
faq.a2: A single post exports at 3×. A very long thread defaults to 2× to stay under the size ceiling; when it would read too small, the panel warns and suggests splitting. A global 3× switch lives in the export settings.
faq.q3: Do I need to log in or connect X?
faq.a3: No. There is no account system: it reads only what the page in front of you has already rendered, and never touches a credential.
faq.a4: No. The image goes to your clipboard and your disk; closing the preview releases the rest. No post content is stored.
faq.a5: The software is GPL-3.0-or-later and free to use commercially. The words and pictures inside a card still belong to their author; check before you redistribute.
faq.a6: Chrome and Edge, from Chrome 111 (Manifest V3). Firefox and Safari are not supported yet: the extension is built on Chromium's extension APIs.
faq.q7: How do I screenshot a tweet without replies?
faq.a7: Click the PostPress card button on the post (or hover and press Alt + C). PostPress reads only that post—or consecutive posts by the same author in a thread—and automatically leaves out ads and third-party replies. If a thread includes a post you want to omit, click once to exclude it before copying.
faq.q8: Can I turn a tweet into a PNG?
faq.a8: Yes. PostPress renders the card locally in your browser and copies a 3× PNG straight to your clipboard (or downloads the PNG file to your disk). Very long threads default to 2× to stay under the size ceiling, with an option in export settings for 3×.

close.sub: Install once, then it sits in the action bar of every post. One click to the clipboard, ready to paste anywhere.
